I was at palmerstown veterinary hospital on a sunday with my elderly cat Igor who has been suffering with feline leukemia. Igor hadn't been eating or drinking or was very weak and we had to send him to cat heaven that day. It was an extremely emotional and difficult day for us, especially to my children who have known Igor all their lives. The vet, nurse and all staff have been extremely compassionate and kind and I have nothing but gratitude for making that day as tolerable as it was. The hand written card with paw prints arrived 2 days after which again was such a lovely gesture. Thank you again for your excellence services.

Service was amazing, very thorough and on time! I got my two bunnies vaccinated and the handling was so gentle with an amazing deal for rabbits which aren’t available anywhere else in Dublin from what IK (rabbit plan)!

Went in on behalf on my friend to collect her ill guinea pig. They know Popcorn so well and you can tell they have love for him. They explained everything to me in easy terms and wrote down all information for me to revert back to the owner. The nurse was brilliant, she took her time and didn’t rush me when I needed clarification. I spoke to a wonderful lady on reception about booking my own guinea pigs for a check up. She was attentive and caring, but she just radiated warmth and passion for the animals. I wasn’t a customer today, just a friend doing a favour, but I’ll most certainly be booking my girls in for a check up. After a long day of work, worrying about my friends guinea pig and rushing down to collect him, I left there absolutely beaming at the interactions I had for my short duration there. Thank you so much girls and thank you for taking such good care of Popcorn.

We visited pvh for the first time this week with our pet Rabbit Winnie who was in terrible pain and in a dangerous situation as she had not eaten for over a week. We travelled 2 hours as knew we needed an experienced vet for Rabbits as had found in the past local vets just didn't have the knowledge necessary for specific Rabbit care. Our journey and time was certainly not wasted as Winnie received excellent care by exotics vet Fiona in pvh and of course the rest of the team. Fiona was so thorough and explained everything so clearly that she found on scans. While there was a few things going on for Winnie, it was decided that we deal with her dental work and get her comfortable and eating again to build her up and revisit the other issues after that.
Well we brought in a very poorly Rabbit but after her care from Fiona and the team we literally have a new very happy Rabbit home again, she is a changed bunny. We are so grateful for the care we got from everyone including Reception in pvh for our little Rabbit, and genuinely so impressed by Fionas knowledge of Rabbits and their specific medical needs including anaesthesia which has to be a tricky thing in these little mammals.
Thank you everyone in pvh, we wouldn't hesitate to recommend this practise to anyone ,  and are very grateful that they could fit us in so quickly this week. Thank you Fiona and team pvh!
I was only walking by the shop but it looked very busy, so must be a good vet there.

We came in there for a snakes stuck eye shed removal & instead they ripped her eyes out.

When we got to the vet they removed what they claimed to be, a "stuck shed" from her eyes and said that they left a little piece of it in the corner that should Fall off on its own. But that was not the concerning part as we got her back after the procedure her eyes were bulged up and looked like two huge balloons that were on each side of her head ( they looked like they were popped out of socket ) but when we asked about that we got told that "this is joust normal" and that we will have to put the eyes drops in her eyes that they gave us
( they gave us two types to give to her ). So we got home and went with the "Doctor's" instructions but after some time her eyes would bleed from time to time after applying the eye drops. Time passed & there was no improvement. We came in on a short notice 2nd time and my Hognose, was treated I believe by an ordinary "Vet" and not an exotic as I was told that the exotic vet is feeling very sick so she cannot speak to me, but I was assured that she was the one that took a good look at her. On that day my snake had its eyes pulled out of a socket, what was left were two flesh wounds in the place where her eyes once were. I was told that they only removed the shed, for the second time??? and that once she sheds fully next tims, her eyes will pop back out, she said they were "hidden" & no they were not! They were already gone! Before we left, which was a cherry on top, that dumb doctor tried to tell me that my snake was a southern hognose instead of a western & I had to correct them, in which they agreed that it was also possible?!? Overall it cost me around 500euro just for my snake to be permanently disfigured, losing both of her eyes by this group of incompetent idiots that will take every penny out of your pocket while lying straight into your face! Didn't get a single cent back, no apolgy & zero accountability.

This happened a year ago and only now I am able to talk about this as this event left a big scar on me. What these people did will forever haunt me.

If someone doesn't belive me, I can send people the full story of what exactly happened & documented images of what happened ( some are pretty graphical ). This is only the shortened version. unfortunately Google Reviews have a word count limit. Don't bring your animals to Palmerstown Veterinary Hospital, or you will be receiving them back slaughtered. :(

Oww and one more thing they claim that she had her eyes visible after leaving, Bull Shit! maybe on her bloody.
tissue. Worst exotic vet ever

I am writing to express my deep concern regarding the care my pet rabbit received in June 2023. I believe the veterinary procedures followed were below standard, particularly due to the absence of necessary blood tests. My rabbit showed signs of infection, yet no blood tests were conducted to investigate underlying health issues. Afterward, she underwent two consecutive procedures to address a swollen eye. Unfortunately, her condition worsened, leading to increased swelling on the right side of her head. I specifically questioned whether these procedures would enable her to close her eye, and I was told, “it might.” Despite being prescribed antibiotics and eye drops intended to lubricate her eye, her condition deteriorated, and she ultimately lost sight in that eye.
The timing of these two procedures was concerning, and I had trusted the expertise of the so-called exotic specialists. However, after seeing no improvement, I sought a second opinion from another vet, as I was extremely disappointed with the care provided.
At a vulnerable time, I relied on the veterinary team's judgment. Tragically, my rabbit passed away weeks later, and I find myself questioning whether timely blood tests might have altered the course of her health. If I had sought a second opinion sooner, she might still be with me.
